# Oregon Records Retention — Agency Special Schedules

> Non-authoritative, AI-friendly reference for the agency-specific *special* records retention schedules published by the Oregon Secretary of State Archives Division.
> Full verbatim text of jurisdiction-authored documents is included in-repo;
> third-party materials are summarized with links to official sources.
> Always verify against the authoritative source linked in each document.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): rules for AI agents working in this corpus
- [STATUS.md](STATUS.md): freshness, coverage, and drift at a glance

## Contents

- `schedules/`: 76 agency **special** records-retention schedules, one Markdown file per
  agency (or per ODOT division), each carrying the full verbatim text of the schedule PDF
  published by the Secretary of State Archives Division. Consult these to answer "how long
  must <agency> keep <record type>, and what happens to it then?" — every record series is
  a numbered item followed by its retention and disposition clause.

## What is NOT here

Oregon's **general** retention schedules — OAR chapter 166, all 15 divisions, 210 rules —
are deliberately absent. They live verbatim in
[OregonAI/executive-regulatory-frameworks](https://github.com/OregonAI/executive-regulatory-frameworks)
and are referenced from here, never copied: two divergent copies of a retention period is
exactly how a record gets destroyed on the strength of the stale one.

A special schedule *supplements* the general schedule for its agency. To answer a
retention question completely you may need both — this corpus, and OAR 166 next door. Each
schedule's `relationships.related` lists the general-schedule rules it cites, as citation
strings such as `OAR 166-300-0015`. Resolving one of those here returns a pointer to the
sibling corpus rather than a document; cross-corpus resolution is not implemented yet.

## Citing

- a whole schedule: `DAS Special Schedule`, or its id `schedule-das`
- a single record series: `DAS Special Schedule item 014` — resolves to the schedule that
  contains it, with the item number carried in the response
